title: Turning any boring homework into a playable game
author: Extension_Run_9597
selftext:
I made a prototype where you can upload a worksheet and it builds a game. This is how it could look like. The workflow doesn't work yet but would love to hear your feedback!

Specs:

* Upload your homework and play through a 3D level generated from your assignments.
* Currently single-player, with a goal of full multiplayer support.
* Built with **Babylon.js** and powered by the **Gemini API** for intelligent data extraction.

Would this actually be useful for your study sessions, or would it just be a distraction? Let me know why!

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: I think it could be a good tool a long as gameplay is not too prioritized over the learning aspect. I think it has to be a balance to do something like that as often it's either more so one or the other. Super great concept tho!

replies.author: Extension_Run_9597
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! Yeah definitely, but that balance is definitely the most difficult part - especially when trying to let the AI do it😅 Still requires a lot handholding

comments.author: ScratchJolly3213
comments.body: Seems great but how does it actually work to adapt to any kind of worksheet?

replies.author: Extension_Run_9597
replies.body: Thanks! Off the shelf, LLMs already do a great job in extracting the subject and information of most worksheets. It's more about embedding the content into a didactical meaningful exercise that is also fun and feels like a game - This is also the tricky part. My approach would be to build a growing library of learning games and guide the AI so it learns what a "good" learning game is

comments.author: drnktgr
comments.body: If I upload a worksheet on manatees, will it make the manatee simulator game?

comments.author: ReaIlmaginary
comments.body: Could be a new age Math Blaster, but you have to make sure the math logic is correct and not “there are 2 r’s in strawberry”

comments.author: kavakravata
comments.body: This is amazing! Mind sharing the initial prompt to set this up? Would love to gamify some aspects of my life as well. Cheers!

comments.author: Opening-Bid4424
comments.body: This is really awesome. Would it be focused on a specific age range / topics? I feel like going too broad will be hard to handle in terms of quality. We’re talking education here so it has to be rock solid.

comments.author: Picture-imp
comments.body:
Cool concept! I’ve been working for several years as a product designer for educational apps with a focus on gamification. I had a very similar idea myself: transforming everyday homework assignments into small games through photo scanning and AI. Because while there are already some pretty good learning apps out there, they don’t really solve the problem that teachers still assign homework in the form of worksheets, which are often not particularly motivating.

I eventually stopped pursuing the idea, though, because I didn’t yet have good solutions for several challenges. That’s why I’m even more excited to see how far you’ve already come with it. What do the games look like for more complex tasks, such as word problems, language subjects, or higher grade levels? Is the AI already good enough to generate a fitting game for every type of task? Quizzes are always possible, of course, but they also become repetitive over time and are already covered by many other apps.

In the end, teachers still want the completed worksheets handed back to them. How do the solutions from the game make their way back onto the worksheet? Even if the games are fun, students probably wouldn’t want to solve everything a second time in their workbooks afterward. Alternatively, the app might need to target teachers directly, so they can scan and upload their worksheets themselves, provide them to students through the app, and then review the results for all students within the app.

The direction you’re taking is promising, but I think the success will depend on whether the app can provide a smooth, frictionless experience from start to finish that keeps students engaged over a longer period of time.

In any case, I wish you the best of luck with it!
